deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the neighbouring folios Riemann is solving the damped (telegraph-type) wave equation. After reduction to characteristic variables this becomes u_pq + u = 0, and he represents its solutions by integrals over a parameter rho. This page has four threads.

(A) Integral representation of e^{...}-type solutions. The top note reads e^{sqrt(pq)}. He considers I = ∫ e^{rho p + q/rho} d rho/rho. Each integrand e^{rho p + q/rho} solves u_pq = u; with i's inserted, as on the next page, it solves u_pq + u = 0.
- He substitutes s = rho p + q/rho - 2 sqrt(pq), which vanishes at the stationary point rho = sqrt(q/p).
- Then ds = (rho p - q/rho) d log rho.
- Also (rho p - q/rho)^2 = (rho p + q/rho)^2 - 4pq = (s + 2 sqrt(pq))^2 - 4pq = s^2 + 4 s sqrt(pq).
- Hence (my completion) I = e^{2 sqrt(pq)} ∫ e^s ds / sqrt(s^2 + 4 s sqrt(pq)), taken twice, once for each branch rho < or > sqrt(q/p). This is the factor e^{2 sqrt} he writes beside the integral.
- In modern terms ∫_0^∞ e^{-(rho p + q/rho)} d rho/rho = 2 K_0(2 sqrt(pq)), and the closed-contour version gives 2πi I_0(2 sqrt(pq)). Equivalently, by the substitution he notes as d(rho sqrt(p/q)), rho p + q/rho = (rho + 1/rho) sqrt(pq). So the solution depends only on sqrt(pq): it is the Riemann/Bessel function of u_pq ± u = 0.

(B) Discontinuous integral (the computation is completed on the next page).
- Delta = ∫_{-∞}^{∞} sin s/s ds (= π).
- The case table records the value of a rho-integral: u = cos(2t)·Delta when x+t>0 and x-t>0, and u = 0 when x+t<0 and x-t<0. The mixed case x+t>0, x-t<0 is listed but left open.
- The integral is ∫_0^∞ sin((rho + 1/rho) sqrt(pq)) [ (q rho + p/rho)/(q rho - p/rho) - (p rho + q/rho)/(p rho - q/rho) ] d log rho.
- Simplifying the bracket (my check): the numerator is (pq rho^2 - q^2 + p^2 - pq/rho^2) - (pq rho^2 - p^2 + q^2 - pq/rho^2) = 2(p^2 - q^2). The denominator is pq(rho^2 + 1/rho^2) - p^2 - q^2.
- Use d log rho = d(rho + 1/rho)/(rho - 1/rho) and s = (rho + 1/rho) sqrt(pq). Then pq(rho^2 + rho^-2) - p^2 - q^2 = s^2 - (p+q)^2 and d(rho + 1/rho)/(rho - 1/rho) = ds / sqrt(s^2 - 4pq).
- rho in (0,∞) covers s in (2 sqrt(pq), ∞) twice. Hence the integral equals 2 ∫_{2 sqrt(pq)}^∞ sin s · 2(p^2 - q^2)/(s^2 - (p+q)^2) · ds/sqrt(s^2 - 4pq). Riemann writes p^2 - q^2 without the 2.
- The integral is Mehler–Sonine-like, with an extra rational factor whose pole s = p+q ≥ 2 sqrt(pq) lies on the path.

(C) Two elliptic differentials: sqrt(pq) d rho / sqrt((q - p rho^2)(q - k^2 p rho^2)) and sqrt(pq) d rho / sqrt((p - q rho^2)(k^2 p - q rho^2)).
- With rho = sigma sqrt(q/p), resp. rho = sigma sqrt(p/q), they become Legendre forms: d sigma / sqrt((1 - sigma^2)(1 - k^2 sigma^2)), resp. d sigma / sqrt((1 - sigma^2)(k^2 - sigma^2)).
- This is a side jotting, probably prompted by the same rho-scaling.

(D) Spherically symmetric telegraph equation: alpha^2 u_tt + u_t = a^2 (u_rr + (2/r) u_r).
- He first notes the standard reduction alpha^2 (ru)_tt + (ru)_t = a^2 (ru)_rr, using (ru)_rr = r u_rr + 2 u_r.
- He then introduces a retarded/advanced time: u = f(tau, r) with tau = t + rho(r) and rho' = alpha/a, i.e. wave speed a/alpha.
- Chain rule: u_r = f_tau rho' + f_r and u_rr = f_tautau rho'^2 + 2 f_rtau rho' + f_tau rho'' + f_rr. Also u_t = f_tau and u_tt = f_tautau.
- Since a^2 rho'^2 = alpha^2 and rho'' = 0, the second-order tau-terms cancel, giving f_tau = 2 a alpha f_rtau + (2 a alpha/r) f_tau + a^2 (f_rr + (2/r) f_r). His (struck) line omits a^2 on the last two terms.
- Rewritten as d/dt(u - 2 a alpha u_r - 2 a alpha u/r) = a^2 (u_rr + (2/r) u_r) (struck out).
- Finally the left side is put in integrating-factor form: u_tau - 2 a alpha u_rtau - 2 a alpha u_tau/r = -2 a alpha (1/r) e^{r/(2 a alpha)} d/dr ( e^{-r/(2 a alpha)} r u_tau ). This exhibits the front amplitude factor e^{-r/(2 a alpha)}, i.e. e^{-t/(2 alpha^2)} on the front.
- Scattered marks (e^{st} - e^{-st}, e^t) are scratch work.

(E) Lower right: a sketch of the complex sigma-plane with marked points ±i, ±sqrt(pq), ±(p+q)/2, -∞, +c, i∞, +1.
- Also written: ∫^{sqrt(pq) i} e^{2 sigma} (x t/(sigma^2 + t^2)) d sigma / sqrt(sigma^2 + pq), with edge contributions -e^{-2 sigma} d sigma and -e^{+2 sigma}(-d sigma) along the cuts.
- This is the contour deformation, completed on the next page, that turns the s-integral of (B), with s = 2 sigma and p+q = 2t, into ∫_{-i sqrt(pq)}^{i sqrt(pq)} e^{2 sigma} xt/(sigma^2 + t^2) d sigma / sqrt(sigma^2 + pq) = 2 ∫_0^{sqrt(pq)} cos 2 sigma · xt/(t^2 - sigma^2) d sigma / sqrt(pq - sigma^2).
- Purpose: evaluate the solution of u_pq + u = 0 (the reduced telegraph equation) with data discontinuous across the characteristics.
errors: The radicand is written as s s + 4 sqrt(pq); the correct value is s s + 4 s sqrt(pq), since (rho p - q/rho)^2 = s^2 + 4 s sqrt(pq). This is either a slip or an ambiguous parenthesis s(s + 4 sqrt(pq)).
In the simplification of the bracket a factor 2 is dropped: the numerator should be 2(p^2 - q^2), not p^2 - q^2. The next page has it correctly (2(p^2-q^2), later 4(p^2-q^2)).

In the final s-integral, the pole s = p+q lies inside the integration range [2 sqrt(pq), ∞), because p+q ≥ 2 sqrt(pq). A principal value or indentation is needed, and this is not indicated here (the contour sketch may address it).
In the struck-out transformed PDE, the terms ∂²u/∂r² + (2/r)∂u/∂r lack the factor a^2 (or a = 1 is tacitly set in only part of the equation).
The case table leaves the mixed case (x+t>0, x-t<0) without a value.

results.what: Integral ∫ e^{rho p + q/rho} d rho/rho reduced by s = rho p + q/rho - 2 sqrt(pq) to e^{2 sqrt(pq)} ∫ e^s ds/sqrt(s^2 + 4 s sqrt(pq)); dependence only on sqrt(pq) via the rho sqrt(p/q) rescaling
results.modern_name: Schläfli/Bessel-type integral representation of I_0, K_0 (J_0) of argument 2 sqrt(pq); Riemann function of u_pq ± u = 0
results.usually_credited_to: Bessel generating function (Bessel 1824, Schlömilch 1857); Schläfli integral 1871; the Riemann function J_0(2 sqrt(pq)) for the telegraph equation is usually attributed to Riemann's method (1860) as worked out by Riemann–Weber, du Bois-Reymond and Picard

results.what: Discontinuous rho-integral equal to π cos 2t in one characteristic quadrant and 0 in the opposite one, reduced to 2∫_{2sqrt(pq)}^∞ sin s · 2(p^2-q^2)/(s^2-(p+q)^2) ds/sqrt(s^2-4pq)
results.modern_name: Discontinuous (Dirichlet/Weber-type) integral; Mehler–Sonine-type representation of a Klein–Gordon/telegraph solution with data jumping across characteristics
results.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet discontinuous factor (1839); Mehler (1868) and Sonine (1880) for ∫ sin(as)/sqrt(s^2-1) ds = (π/2) J_0(a); Weber (1873) for discontinuous Bessel integrals

results.what: Telegraph equation with spherical symmetry: reduction via r u, and retarded-time substitution tau = t + (alpha/a) r cancelling second tau-derivatives, with integrating-factor form exhibiting e^{-r/(2 a alpha)} front damping
results.modern_name: Telegraph (damped wave) equation; transport/eikonal reduction along characteristics, front attenuation
results.usually_credited_to: Kirchhoff 1857 (telegraph equation); Heaviside 1876; Poincaré 1893 and Picard 1894 (solution)

results.what: Normalisation of two elliptic differentials to Legendre form by rho = sigma sqrt(q/p) or sqrt(p/q)
results.modern_name: Legendre normal form of elliptic integrals of the first kind

deep.surprise_reason: The page belongs to Riemann's known circle of work: the Riemann method for hyperbolic equations (1860) and electrodynamics/retarded potentials (1858). The Bessel-type Riemann function and the telegraph equation are associated with him through Riemann–Weber. The explicit discontinuous integral with a Mehler–Sonine-type reduction, and the contour evaluation for u_pq+u=0, are a notable unpublished detail predating Mehler/Sonine and Poincaré/Picard. They are fragmentary and close to what his method naturally produces, so modest surprise.

checkable.asserts: the correct radicand is s^2 + 4 s sqrt(pq) (should be 0)
bracket simplifies to 2(p^2-q^2)/(pq(rho^2+rho^-2)-p^2-q^2) (should be 0; Riemann drops the 2 here)
denominator equals s^2-(p+q)^2 with s=(rho+1/rho)sqrt(pq) (should be 0)
rho-1/rho = sqrt(s^2-4pq)/sqrt(pq), so dlog rho = ds/sqrt(s^2-4pq) (should be 0)
integrating-factor form of the left side, with g = u_tau (should be 0)
substituting u=f(t+(alpha/a)r, r) cancels f_tautau (check manually that the alpha^2 f_tautau terms cancel)
∫_0^∞ e^{-(rho p+q/rho)} d rho/rho = 2K_0(2sqrt(pq)) for p=2,q=3 (≈0)
Mehler–Sonine: ∫_{2sqrt(pq)}^∞ sin s ds/sqrt(s^2-4pq) = (π/2)J_0(2sqrt(pq)), pq=6 (≈0, conditionally convergent)
first elliptic differential reduces to Legendre form under rho=sigma sqrt(q/p) (should be 0)

transcription_corrections: Top line: the radicand should read √(s s + 4 s √pq) (or √(s(s+4√pq))), not √(s s + 4√pq); the same applies in ∫ e^s ds/√(...).
The integral defining Delta is ∫_{-∞}^{∞} sin s/s ds = Δ (limits -∞ to ∞).
The bottom expression is (1/r) e^{r/(2aα)} ∂(e^{-r/(2aα)} r ∂u/∂τ)/∂r, multiplied by the factor -2aα written beneath it, not a separate entry.
In the struck-out line the coefficient reads 2αa ∂²u/∂r∂τ + αa (∂u/∂τ)(2/r) + ...; the a^2 factor is absent in the manuscript itself.
The ∫ e^{2σ} xt/(σ²+t²) dσ/√(σ²+pq) fragment belongs with the contour sketch (limits ±√pq·i), linked to the next page.
